The Separable 3D Transfer Function Editor is a user interface technique that decomposes a 3D transfer function space into a primary 2D domain and associated 1D domains to improve usability while maintaining classification precision [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states that the proposed method separates a 3D transfer function space into a 2D domain and associated 1D domains. It confirms that this separation is designed to improve usability (by leveraging familiar 2D interaction and providing histograms for 1D refinement) while attempting to maintain classification precision (by using combination selection rules to mitigate precision loss from dependent spaces). All specific details in the claim are present in the source text.
supported
*   **Mitigation:** Combination selection rules rule out highly dependent 1D transfer function spaces to preserve precision [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states in Section 3.1.3 that 'our combination selection rules proposed in Section 3.1.2 help to rule out highly dependent 1D transfer function spaces' to mitigate decreased classification precision caused by the separation of the 3D space into 2D and 1D domains. This directly supports the claim that combination selection rules rule out highly dependent 1D transfer function spaces to preserve precision.

It addresses the difficulty of interacting with true 3D transfer function widgets by allowing users to define regions in a 2D space (e.g., scalar vs. gradient magnitude) and then refine classification using a tertiary attribute (e.g., occlusion) via a linked 1D editor [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states that true 3D transfer function widgets are difficult to interact with and proposes a method that separates the space into a 2D domain (e.g., scalar vs. gradient magnitude) and associated 1D domains. It confirms that users define regions in the 2D space using widgets (including a lasso tool) and then refine classification using a tertiary attribute (e.g., occlusion) via a linked 1D editor that displays the histogram for the selected region.
